ledger.x: c. 2070 BC: the Xia begins, traditionally under Yu the Great. Infobox 'Established: c. 2070 BC'; the Xia-Shang-Zhou Chronology Project 'proposed that the Xia existed between 2070 and 1600 BC' (other chronologies: Liu Xin 2205-1766, Bamboo Annals 1989-1558). Yu is 'the likely legendary figure'; the land is the…

c. 1750 BC: the Erlitou culture spreads over Henan and Shanxi. The page gives the culture 1750-1500 BC (radiocarbon since 2007) and its extent 'throughout Henan and Shanxi', but dates no stage of the spread, so the year is the start of the revised range, a bridge.

c. 1600 BC: Tang overthrows Jie and the Shang succeed the Xia. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1600 BC', 'Successor: Shang dynasty'; Jie 'was overthrown by Tang, who inaugurated the new Shang dynasty' (no date for the overthrow; the Chronology Project links it to the walled cities at Yanshi and Zhengzhou c. 1600 BC).…

wars.name: Overthrow of Jie by Tang
wars.outcome: Jie, the last Xia ruler, 'was overthrown by Tang, who inaugurated the new Shang dynasty'; the page gives no date, battle or territorial detail (the Battle of Mingtiao is not mentioned on the page; the shang-dynasty dossier names it).

certainty.note: No Xia boundary exists in the pages; the Erlitou distribution is archaeological.
